payload.because: Operator decision for the whole app: never hard-delete traveller-made data, never ask "are you sure?", POST /api/undo restores the latest deletion, deleted things never appear in any list, total or suggestion. A journal with deletion_id groups cascades (e.g. deleting a trip with its days) so one undo restores them together.
payload.chose: App-wide soft delete + undo: every traveller-made table gets `deleted_at TEXT` and `deletion_id INTEGER` columns; a DELETE writes one row to a `deletions` journal (id AUTOINCREMENT, kind, entity_id, label, deleted_at, undone_at) and stamps every affected row (including future cascades) with that deletion_id. POST /api/undo restores the most recent not-yet-undone deletion (a stack: repeated undo walks back further) by clearing deleted_at/deletion_id in every table registered in SOFT_DELETE_TABLES (apps/web/lib/server/deletions.ts), returns 200 { restored: { kind, id, label } }; 409 nothing_to_undo when the journal has nothing left. All reads filter `deleted_at IS NULL`. No confirmation dialogs in the UI; an Undo button is offered after deleting instead.
payload.over: Hard DELETE; confirm dialogs; per-entity undo endpoints; a single deleted flag without a journal (cannot order undo or group cascades)
payload.rule: Never hard-delete traveller-made rows or add confirm dialogs: soft-delete via lib/server/deletions.ts (register the table in SOFT_DELETE_TABLES) and filter `deleted_at IS NULL` in every list, total and suggestion.

Wrap handlers with `handle<C>()` from apps/web/lib/server/api.ts (context is optional in the returned type so tests can call `GET(new Request(url))`); for `[id]` routes use `handle<IdContext>` and tests pass `{ params: Promise.resolve({ id }) }`. Typing the context as `void` breaks the build typecheck.

payload.summary: Built piece 2, the bucket list, plus the app-wide rule that deletes are soft and can be undone (D6). Migration v2 appends a `deletions` journal and a `bucket_items` table with deleted_at and deletion_id columns. lib/server/deletions.ts has softDelete(target), which journals the delete and stamps rows (it handles cascades and returns false with nothing written when no row matched). It also has undoLatestDeletion(), which restores the latest deletion not yet undone across SOFT_DELETE_TABLES and throws 409 nothing_to_undo when there is none. lib/server/bucket.ts does list, get, create, partial PATCH and soft delete, with validation: title trimmed to 1–200 chars; city_id a provider city id or null, unknown gives 400; notes up to 2000 chars; estimated_daily_spend as Money via the new shared lib/server/validate.ts parseMoneyField, which profile now uses too. Routes: GET/POST /api/bucket (POST returns 201), GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/bucket/[id] (DELETE returns 204, unknown or deleted ids 404), and POST /api/undo, which returns {restored:{kind,entity_id,label,deleted_at}}. api.ts handle<C>() now passes the route context (IdContext). db.ts gains transaction(). GET /api/reference gains cities. The /bucket page is a server page plus the client components/bucket-list.tsx, with testids bucket-item-{id}, bucket-add and bucket-delete-{id}, plus an Undo button (bucket-undo) and field testids. parseAmountInput moved to lib/money.ts. The home page links to /bucket and the README documents the API. There are 39 tests (13 new in test/bucket-api.test.ts). lint, typecheck, test and build are all green, and the full CRUD, undo and 409 flow plus the page were smoke-tested under `next start` on Node.
